title: Bear's on Fairfield
venue_description:
Shreveport's Premier Neighborhood Live Music Venue

Bear's on Fairfield is located at the corner of Fairfield and Southern Avenue inside the Alvin Building in Shreveport's Highland neighborhood. This locally owned establishment serves as one of the city's favorite watering holes and cultural centers for local visual and musical artists. Reopened in 2017 by owner Colton Johnson the venue was originally established in the late 1990s and has survived the test of time through community support.

Live Music and Entertainment Programming

Bear's hosts open jams on Thursday nights featuring indie rock hip-hop songwriters and more. Live local music performances occur most Friday and Saturday nights. The venue also features karaoke and trivia events throughout the week. Music genres typically include indie rock hip-hop songwriters and contemporary local artists. All events showcase the diverse talents of Shreveport's creative community.

Venue Features and Amenities

The venue features great sound equipment and professional sound engineers dedicated to providing quality live music experiences. Locally produced art adorns the walls creating an inviting and creative ambiance. Bear's offers a full menu of food and drinks including handcrafted cocktails wines and spirits. Standout menu items include bacon-wrapped hot dogs and cheeseburgers that have earned enthusiastic praise. The atmosphere is laid back eclectic and welcoming to all walks of life.

Venue Hours and Operations

Bear's operates with extended hours seven days a week. Sunday through Thursday 5:00 PM to 2:00 AM. Friday and Saturday 5:00 PM to 3:00 AM. The late-night operations provide a safe environment for artists musicians and community members. Parking is available on site.

Community and Artist Support

Bear's is much more than a dive bar it is a community hub and safe late-night environment for local talent. Owner Johnson is committed to supporting local visual and musical artists providing them with quality stage space sound production and development opportunities. The venue hosts Bear's Fest annually in May as a local music art food and drinks mini-festival celebrating what Bear's is all about. The owner's vision has been to raise the bar for neighborhood dive bars and elevate expectations of what Shreveport brings to the community.

title: The Historic Korner Lounge
venue_description:
Downtown Shreveport's Cultural Entertainment Hub

The Historic Korner Lounge is located at 800 Louisiana Avenue in downtown Shreveport making it accessible in the heart of the city's cultural district. This legendary venue has become a cornerstone of downtown entertainment featuring vibes as legendary as the performances that grace its stage.

Weekly Entertainment and Open Mics

The Korner Lounge hosts open mic comedy nights on Thursday evenings starting at 8:00 PM with sign-up beginning at 7:00 PM. Sunday nights feature casual karaoke with the microphone opening at 7:00 PM. Both events are completely free with no cover charge providing accessible entertainment to all community members. Happy hour specials run from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily making it an affordable destination.

Performer and Audience Experience

The venue welcomes performers of all skill levels whether seasoned comedians testing new material or first-timers ready to try stand-up for the first time. The stage is open and welcoming. As an audience member attendees enjoy a night of laughter creativity and community connection. The intimate setting builds strong connections between performers and audiences.

Venue Hours and Atmosphere

The Historic Korner Lounge operates from 5:00 PM to 12:00 AM most evenings creating an evening and late-night entertainment destination. The venue features quality sound systems and stage production capabilities. Patrons can enjoy cocktails and refreshments while experiencing performances. The overall atmosphere emphasizes good vibes great tunes and community celebration.

Location and Accessibility

Situated in downtown Shreveport the Korner Lounge is easily accessible and serves as an anchor for downtown entertainment programming. The venue plays an important role in supporting emerging talent and maintaining Shreveport's vibrant cultural scene. Its commitment to free or low-cost entertainment ensures accessibility to diverse audiences throughout the community.

title: Louisiana Grandstand
venue_description:
Historic Music Venue and American Roots Music Center

The Louisiana Grandstand is housed in the historic Woman's Department Club building constructed in 1925. Located at 802 Margaret Place at the corner of Line Avenue and Margaret Place in the Highland/Stoner area just south of downtown this beautiful restored building is known affectionately as the Lady on Line. The building was designed by architect Clarence F. King and stands alongside the famous Strand Theater as one of the two oldest theaters in current-day Shreveport/Bossier City.

Venue Spaces and Theater History

The Louisiana Grandstand operates two intimate music performance spaces: the Legendary Listening Room with 400 capacity and The Listening Lounge with 75 capacity. Both feature exceptional acoustics with no bad seats in the house ensuring intimate performance experiences. The WDC Theater was originally built by the Woman's Department Club as a 400-plus seat theater on the second floor used for lectures performances and club events. The theater has hosted legendary figures including Robert Frost Katharine Hepburn and First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt.

Contemporary Programming and Artist Development

The Louisiana Grandstand was founded in 2019 to grow and innovate the American Roots music scene in Northwest Louisiana building on the foundation of the legendary Louisiana Hayride radio broadcast. The venue hosts a diverse schedule including touring artists regional talent showcases and artist development programming. A requirement for major bookings is that local Shreveport musicians must be included as show openers fostering local talent. The venue operates an onsite recording studio providing local artists with studio time and production resources.

Artist Ambassador Program

The 2025 Louisiana Grandstand Artist Ambassador Program pairs established music mentors with emerging local artist mentees for one calendar year. The inaugural mentors include Shreveport natives Kix Brooks one half of the iconic duo Brooks and Dunn and current country hitmaker Jordan Davis. This program reflects the venue's commitment to fostering grassroots music development.

Venue Features and Services

The venue emphasizes an acoustics-first intimate performance environment that values storytelling songwriting and live musicianship. Each performance is elevated with video presentations to enhance the visual experience. An upstairs concession area is complemented by the Louisiana Grandstand mobile app allowing patrons to order food and drinks to their seats at no additional charge. The venue offers validated parking and provides attentive personable hospitality. Every seat offers excellent views of the stage.

Historic Significance and Restoration

After struggling with COVID-19 impacts the Woman's Department Club partnered with Louisiana Grandstand in 2020 to restore the historic building. Restoration work includes a new roof installation and cosmetic improvements beginning in 2022. The Woman's Department Club remains active today meeting every Thursday with various programs and exhibits. The venue continues to preserve this important historic landmark while elevating it as a premier music center in Shreveport/Bossier City.

title: Brookshire Grocery Arena
venue_description:
Louisiana's Premier Large-Venue Entertainment Destination

Brookshire Grocery Arena is located at 2000 Brookshire Arena Drive in Bossier City Louisiana on the banks of the Red River. This state-of-the-art 270,000 square foot facility opened in late 2000 and has established itself as one of the top entertainment destinations in the South capable of hosting up to 14,000 patrons.

Venue Capabilities and Programming

The arena hosts world-class concerts family shows ice-skating shows motor sports events rodeos conventions religious gatherings and diverse community programs. Major events include the annual Shreveport Blues Festival celebrating Southern soul and blues music and Winter Fest featuring hip-hop celebration performances. The venue features modern sound systems and production capabilities supporting large-scale entertainment experiences.

Music and Entertainment History

Brookshire Grocery Arena has hosted performances by major touring artists and regional talent across multiple genres including blues country soul rock and hip-hop. The annual Shreveport Blues Festival features performances by regional and national artists continuing Shreveport's strong blues heritage rooted in the legendary Louisiana Hayride era. The Winter Fest celebration brings together major recording artists for high-energy hip-hop performances.

Location and Facilities

Conveniently located within the Shreveport-Bossier entertainment district the arena provides easy access from approximately 12,000 hotel rooms five casinos and numerous local restaurants. The facility provides ample parking and modern amenities for attendees. Professional venue management by ASM Global ensures quality operations across diverse event types.

Community Impact

As Louisiana's premier large-venue entertainment facility Brookshire Grocery Arena plays a vital role in the regional cultural and entertainment landscape. The venue supports musical traditions while hosting contemporary touring acts that appeal to diverse audiences. Its presence as a major entertainment venue contributes to the regional economy and cultural vitality of the Shreveport-Bossier metropolitan area.
location: 2000 Brookshire Arena Drive Bossier City LA 71112

title: Hurricane Alley Live
venue_description:
Louisiana's Top Outdoor Live Music Venue

Hurricane Alley Live is an outdoor concert venue located in Bossier City within the East Bank District. This vibrant entertainment venue features multiple dining and entertainment options including restaurants axe-throwing activities and a dedicated outdoor live music stage.

Entertainment Programming and Music Genres

Hurricane Alley Live specializes in hosting live music performances Thursday through Saturday. The venue features diverse music genres including Red Dirt Country classic rock Cajun Zydeco and tribute bands. The venue's programming emphasizes regional and touring artists that appeal to Shreveport-Bossier audiences.

Venue Layout and Amenities

The outdoor venue includes multiple bars dining areas indoor and outdoor seating heated courtyards and stage areas. The setting provides flexibility for various entertainment experiences with options to enjoy food and drinks while experiencing live performances. The venue welcomes families and dogs creating a diverse and inclusive atmosphere.

Location and Accessibility

Hurricane Alley Live is conveniently located within walking distance of approximately 12,000 hotel rooms five casinos and the area's top local restaurants. As part of Bossier City's East Bank District the venue benefits from proximity to major entertainment and hospitality infrastructure. The East Bank District is one of only three open container districts in Louisiana allowing patrons to enjoy beverages while walking through the entertainment area.

Event Features

The venue offers fantastic stage production and professional sound systems. Special events include New Year's Eve celebrations featuring fireworks. The outdoor setting with heated elements provides year-round entertainment options. The venue's versatility and multiple entertainment options make it a comprehensive entertainment destination within the region.
location: East Bank District Bossier City LA 71111
